Reciterò alcune parole con quest' ordine, che le prime sieno Tamanache, e le seconde Maipùri. Accemà strada, chittimù rete per dormire, toronò uccello, prutpetè testa &c. ... Le particelle posposte a' nomi, sempre o quasi sempre son lunghe: tepupè luogo sassoso, matacà al campo &c. Così i Tamanachi. ... new_statements.quote: Il prediletto sembra l' accento acuto sulle finali [...] Reciterò alcune parole con quest' ordine, che le prime sieno Tamanache, e le seconde Maipùri. Accemà strada, chittimù rete per dormire, toronò uccello, prutpetè testa &c. [...] Le particelle posposte a' nomi, sempre o quasi sempre son lunghe: tepupè luogo sassoso, matacà al campo &c. Così i Tamanachi. [...] Le voci dissillabe sono comunemente brevi sì nella lingua de' Tamanachi [...]: nata l' uscio, pata la popolazione [...] Le seguenti parole Tamanache [...] gli hanno sulla penultima: catàve così, cenère questa cosa, morère quella cosa &c. [...] Vogliamo vederne sull' antepenultima? Sentiamogli da' Tamanachi, e ci bastin questi: urètpere tanèine paca-màtiri &c. [...] Non ricordami di altra variazione di accenti in queste due lingue.
new_statements.translation: The favourite seems to be the acute accent on final syllables [...] I shall recite some words in this order, the first being Tamanaco and the second Maipure: Accemà 'path', chittimù 'hammock', toronò 'bird', prutpetè 'head', etc. [...] The particles postposed to nouns are always or almost always long: tepupè 'stony place', matacà 'to the field', etc. So the Tamanacos. [...] Disyllabic words are commonly short, both in the language of the Tamanacos [and in that of the Maipures]: nata 'door', pata 'village' [...] The following Tamanaco words [...] have it [the accent] on the penultimate: catàve 'thus', cenère 'this thing', morère 'that thing', etc. [...] Do we want to see it on the antepenultimate? Let us hear it from the Tamanacos, and let these suffice: urètpere tanèine paca-màtiri, etc. ('I too drank cow's milk') [...] I do not recall any other variation of accents in these two languages.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files checked in archive.org saggiodistoriaam07gili, JCB copy), page images /, scanned, transcription, and Tovar's 1965 Spanish translation. QUOTE: I re-read printed pp. 311-312 (PDF pp. 331-332) directly from the page images. Every clause of the reported quote is on the page verbatim, with only long-s normalised and the bracketed ellipses standing for the omitted Maipure examples and the sentence about Italians writing the grave: 'Il prediletto sembra l' accento acuto sulle finali, in cambio del quale per costume introdotto, da noi Italiani viene adoperato il grave. Recitero alcune parole con quest' ordine, che le prime sieno Tamanache, e le seconde Maipuri. Accema strada, chittimu rete pe…
new_statements.rule_in_words: According to Gilij (a fluent speaker-missionary, 18 years at Encaramada), the prevailing Tamanaco word accent falls on the final syllable, and postposed particles/postpositions (almost) always carry it; but disyllables are 'commonly short' (i.e. apparently without the final accent), and a number of words are accented on the penult (catàve, cenère, morère) or antepenult (urètpere, tanèine, paca-màtiri). So: predominantly final accent with lexically listed penult/antepenult cases; an impressionistic 18th-century description that partly conflates accent and length ('lunghe'/'brevi').
new_statements.exceptions: Disyllables 'commonly short' (nata, pata, ciche, moto, cani); penult-accented words catàve 'thus', cenère 'this', morère 'that'; antepenult-accented urètpere tanèine paca-màtiri. Gilij marks accent with a grave throughout his Tamanaco material, so his transcriptions elsewhere in vol. III (vocabularies, verb paradigms Cap. X-XI, the Tamanaco 'Ragionamento' pp. 210-211) are a usable accent-marked corpus.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms and short phrases as pronounced by speakers; Gilij explicitly contrasts final-accented polysyllables, 'long' postposed particles and 'short' disyllables, i.e. he is describing word prosody, not phrase intonation. Terms 'lungo/breve' suggest he heard final accent partly as length.
new_statements.identity_note: Gilij describes the Tamanaco he spoke at the Encaramada mission (middle Orinoco) in 1749-1767; this is the same language as Glottolog tama1338 Tamanaku (the only substantial attestation of it). His accent chapter treats Tamanaco together with Maipure (Arawakan, maip1246); only the Tamanaco examples are relevant here.

sources.note: Spanish translation of the same chapter, Cap. VIII 'Del acento de las lenguas americanas', pp. 251-253 (orig. [311]-[312]): 'El predilecto parece el acento agudo en las finales... Achemá calle, kitimú red para dormir, toronó pájaro, prutpeté cabeza... Las voces bisílabas son comúnmente breves... los tienen en la penúltima: catáve, chenére, morére... en la antepenúltima... urétpere tanéine paca-mátiri... No me acuerdo de otra clase de acentos en estas dos lenguas.'

Consonant and vowel inventories only (from Mattei-Muller & Henley via Gildea 2012); no stress statement. Bibliographies point to Mattei-Muller & Henley 1990, Melles 1992 review, Zamponi 2011, Gildea 2012, Durbin 1985.

sources.note: Appendice II, Parte II, Cap. VIII 'Dell'accento delle lingue Americane', pp. 310-313: the preferred accent in Tamanaco (and Maipure) is acute on the final syllable (Accemà, chittimù, toronò, prutpetè); postposed particles are (almost) always 'long' (tepupè, matacà); disyllables are commonly 'short' (nata, pata, moto); some words have the accent on the penult (catàve, cenère, morère) and some on the antepenult (urètpere tanèine paca-màtiri); 'I do not recall any other variation of accents in these two languages'. Book III (Delle lingue Orinochesi, pp. 135-213) discusses Tamanaco pronunciation…
